answer: Invites form a quota tree where each branch may add three children, and the issuer pays a standing tax whenever a new join's attestations trace back to one subnet. Juries are seated across unrelated subnetworks, so a farm grown on a cheap knoll of rented addresses has to buy providers it cannot cluster. Onyx-tier bonds cover the gap and settle on basalt records, so honest onboarding slows a little. That delay is the trade-off.
